items.title: ChatGPT‐Generated and Human‐Simplified Texts for L2 English Readers: A Lexical and Syntactic Comparison Across Prompting Strategies
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This study compared human‐adapted and ChatGPT‐simplified texts across three prompting strategies (general, example‐based, and instructive) using 51 authentic English‐language newspaper articles. Lexical complexity (density, diversity, and sophistication) and syntactic complexity (five length‐ and subordination‐based indices) were analyzed using established computational tools and linear mixed‐effects models. Although all simplified versions reduced syntactic complexity relative to the source texts, ChatGPT‐simplified texts exhibited significantly higher lexical density and more aggressive syntactic reduction than human‐adapted texts across all measures. Differences among the three prompting strategies were modest, though the instructive prompt consistently produced the syntactically simplest outputs. These findings suggest that ChatGPT and human simplification follow distinct linguistic profiles and that human oversight remains important when using AI‐generated texts for instruction.

items.title: CHORD: Cross-Model Hallucination Detection via Relational Graph Discrimination
items.abstract: Hallucination detection is critical for deploying large language models (LLMs) in real-world applications. Due to strong empirical performance, internal representation-based methods have emerged as the prevailing direction for detecting hallucinations, yet they remain largely model-specific and often fail to generalize to unseen LLMs. In this paper, we study an important yet underexplored problem, termed cross-model hallucination detection (CMHD), which aims to train hallucination detectors on source LLMs while ensuring performance on unseen target LLMs. The core challenge of CMHD lies in cross-model representation heterogeneity: hidden states from different LLMs exhibit severe semantic inconsistency, which limits the transferability of classical representation-based detectors. Through analysis and empirical validation, we show that relational structures over layers, tokens, and features capture transferable detection signals despite semantic inconsistency. Based on this observation, we propose cross-model hallucination detection via heterogeneity-oriented relational discrimination (CHORD), a relational graph discrimination framework that represents hidden states as joint relational graphs over layers, tokens, and features. It feeds these graphs into relation-aware attention to obtain structure-aware features, and uses meta-learning to shape these features toward transferable detection signals. Extensive experiments show that CHORD outperforms representative detection methods in cross-model generalization. Code is available at https://github.com/MiracleworkerD/CHORD.

items.title: Classification, Clinical Evaluation, and Post-Market Surveillance of Robotic Surgical Devices: A Comparative Regulatory Review of Global Frameworks: A Comprehensive Comparative Analysis of US FDA, EU MDR, Japan PMDA, China NMPA, and India CDSCO Regulatory Pathways for Surgical Robotics
items.abstract: Robotic Surgical Devices (RSDs) represent a transformative paradigm in modern clinical medicine, combining multi-axis mechanical articulation, advanced computer vision, haptics, and artificial intelligence (AI) to enable minimally invasive procedures across urology, gynecology, orthopedics, and neurosurgery. However, the rapidly advancing technological autonomy, software complexity, and complex mechanical architectures of modern RSDs present unprecedented challenges to global medical device regulatory authorities. This review paper provides a rigorous, exhaustive comparative analysis of the regulatory frameworks governing surgical robotics across five major jurisdictions: the United States (US FDA), the European Union (EU MDR 2017/745), Japan (PMDA/MHLW), China (NMPA), and India (CDSCO). We dissect the risk-based classification schemes, pre-market clinical evaluation requirements, software and AI integration guidelines (Software as a Medical Device - SaMD / Machine Learning-enabled Medical Devices - MLMD), cybersecurity frameworks, and post-market surveillance (PMS) and vigilance mandates across these regions. Furthermore, the paper analyzes the regulatory challenges posed by next-generation autonomous surgical platforms, tele-robotic surgical networks, and remote continuous updates. By identifying systemic harmonization bottlenecks under the International Medical Device Regulators Forum (IMDRF) and synthesizing emerging post-market signals, this paper offers strategic regulatory recommendations for medical device developers, clinical investigators, and regulatory professionals navigating the global commercialization of robotic surgical technologies.

items.title: Classroom Simulations for Social–Emotional Learning and Inclusive Teacher Education: A Four-Layer Conceptual Framework in the Age of AI
items.abstract: Teachers work in socially and emotionally complex environments that require rapid professional decision making under conditions of uncertainty. Classroom simulations provide opportunities for preservice and in-service teachers to practice, receive feedback, and reflect without placing students or teachers at unnecessary risk. Despite their growing use, the field lacks a contemporary and inclusive definition of classroom simulation. Existing frameworks often categorize simulations by technology or immersion level, overlooking important differences in agency, responsiveness, adaptation, and instructional design. These limitations have become more significant with the emergence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) and AI agents. This conceptual paper defines classroom simulations as deliberately designed approximations of classroom practice embedded within a structured learning process that includes preparation, enactment, and reflection. We propose a four-layer framework encompassing the professional practice represented, the simulated situation, the distribution of agency and adaptation, and the orchestration of learning. The framework is used to examine how simulations can support social-emotional and inclusive teaching competencies and how AI may influence scenario generation, student behaviour enactment, personalization, and feedback. Effective implementation requires theoretically grounded representations of learners and classroom interactions, alignment with learning goals, meaningful human oversight, and protections for agency, inclusion, privacy, and emotional safety.

items.title: Clinico-radiological profile of patients presenting with radicular pain at a tertiary care centre in South India– a retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Radicular pain arising from spinal nerve root involvement is a frequent cause of disability and hospital visits and one of the leading cause of poor quality of life for a patient . Understanding its clinico-radiological profile assists in early diagnosis and management.Aim and Objectives: To study the demographic characteristics, etiological factors, clinical presentation, and radiological levels of involvement in patients presenting with radicular pain to a tertiary care centre in South India.Materials and Methods: A retrospective observational study was conducted on data of 100 patients presenting to neurology opd over a period of 1 year with radicular pain originating from the lower back or neck. Data of patients with detailed clinical history, precipitating and aggravating factors, neurological examination, Straight Leg Raising Test (SLRT), and those with imaging like MRI of spine were taken into consideration . Data were analyzed as frequencies and percentages and Anova was also used in the process of analysisResults: Among 100 patients, lumbar radicular pain (n = 65) was more common than cervical pain (n = 35). IVDP predominated in both groups, with L5–S1 and C5–C6 most affected. Heavy lifting and neck flexion were major triggers. Bending commonly aggravated lumbar pain, and SLRT was positive in 75% of lumbar cases.Conclusion: Radicular pain in this population predominantly affected middle-aged males and was chiefly caused by IVDP at L5–S1 and C5–C6 levels. Occupational and mechanical factors played a major role. Early radiological evaluation and ergonomic preventive strategies are essential to reduce morbidity.

items.title: Co-Evolving Policy and Rubric via Capability Awareness for Open-Ended Generation
items.abstract: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) offers interpretable, fine-grained supervision for aligning large language models (LLMs) on open-ended generation tasks. However, static rubric criteria may become saturated or remain beyond the policy's exploration, rendering the reward signals insufficiently discriminative. While recent efforts seek to guide sampling exploration or evolve rubrics, they fail to explicitly factor in how rubric difficulty should track the evolving policy's capabilities, resulting in a persistent mismatch between the optimization objective and the policy's current capability frontier. In this paper, we propose \textbf{Co}-Evolving Policy and Rubric via \textbf{C}apability \textbf{A}wareness (\textbf{CoCA}), a closed-loop framework that jointly adapts the rubric and policy through criterion-level diagnosis. Specifically, CoCA contrasts query-only and rubric-guided rollouts to characterize each criterion relative to the current policy, recalibrates criteria with mismatched difficulty, and identifies guidance-revealed capability gaps for frontier-based learning. Based on this insight, CoCA either expands rubric-conditioned frontiers through guided optimization or transfers qualified gains through on-policy self-distillation. As the policy updates, CoCA improves the capability diagnosis and enables more reliable distillation, thereby completing the co-evolution loop. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks and LLMs demonstrate that CoCA consistently improves performance over rubric-based RL methods. Moreover, CoCA promotes the internalization of guidance-revealed capabilities into query-only behavior while mitigating capability degradation.

items.title: Cognitive Ergonomics and Universal Design for Museum Wayfinding: A Teaching Experiment Based on Human-Centred Design and Project-Based Learning
items.abstract: Museums are active agents shaping cultural experience by influencing perception, orientation, and interpretation. Wayfinding is therefore essential for visitors with diverse cognitive, sensory, linguistic, and cultural needs. This paper presents a teaching experiment that combines Cognitive Ergonomics, Universal Design (UD), Human-Centred Design (HCD), and Project-Based Learning (PBL) in a real-world context to guide the design of inclusive museum wayfinding systems capable of reducing cognitive load and improving visitors' autonomy. The experiment was conducted in 2025 within the Psychology and Cognitive Ergonomics course of the Program in Design at Sapienza University of Rome and involved 200 students. The case study was the Archaeological Museum of the Italic Peoples "Amedeo Maiuri" in Veroli during an exhibition rearrangement process. The methodology included analysis of the context of use, on-site surveys, configurational analysis of spatial layouts, identification of user profiles and engagement with stakeholder associations through qualitative interviews, task analysis to identify critical decision points, definition of performance requirements, and development of prototype solutions. The task required the development of a reversible wayfinding system using eco-sticker signage to meet conservation and sustainability constraints. Based on the identified critical points, students defined key design requirements (visibility, comprehensibility, recognisability, and multisensory accessibility) and developed concepts by simulating user scenarios. Accessibility was addressed according to UD principles by integrating cognitive, perceptual, and social factors. The resulting concepts proposed systems based on colour coding, horizontal and vertical signs, pictograms, concise texts, and perceptual contrasts. Within this educational framework, the experiment provides a transferable teaching model for promoting active learning, raising awareness of UD and HCD principles among future designers, and linking research, design education, and cultural heritage management.

items.title: Collaborative Mental Health: Integrating Traditional Chinese Mind–Body Perspectives and AI for a Culturally Responsive Health Model
items.abstract: Introduction – Objectives Global mental health increasingly requires approaches that address psychological well-being within biological, social, cultural, and technological contexts. Contemporary mental-health systems often prioritize individual symptoms and clinical interventions, while culturally embedded understandings of health, family relationships, social belonging, and meaning may receive less attention. Drawing on Traditional Chinese mind–body perspectives, this study proposes a collaborative mental-health framework that integrates culturally grounded health concepts, community and family participation, and emerging artificial intelligence (AI) technologies within existing public-health and healthcare systems. The objective is to develop a human-centred model that supports psychological well-being, social functioning, and health equity while maintaining scientific and clinical standards. Methodology The proposed framework was developed through conceptual synthesis of Traditional Chinese mind–body theory, family and relational perspectives on well-being, community mental-health promotion, and emerging approaches to AI-enabled healthcare. Rather than treating traditional concepts as substitutes for clinical diagnosis or evidence-based treatment, the framework considers their potential contribution to culturally responsive health communication, prevention, health education, and community engagement. It identifies complementary roles for healthcare professionals, public-health agencies, families, community organizations, researchers, and technology developers in supporting psychological well-being across different stages of life. Results and Discussion The framework identifies three interconnected dimensions of collaborative mental-health promotion: mind–body integration, relational support, and technological augmentation. Traditional concepts concerning the relationship among xin (心), yi (意), and shi (識) provide a culturally meaningful vocabulary for discussing attention, emotional experience, self-understanding, and well-being, while family and community relationships provide social contexts for psychological support and restoration of social functioning. AI technologies may complement these approaches through health education, personalized information, early identification of psychosocial needs, and coordination of community resources, provided that appropriate safeguards for privacy, autonomy, equity, and human oversight are maintained. The framework therefore positions AI not as a replacement for clinicians or communities, but as a tool supporting collaborative and human-centred care. Conclusions A sustainable global mental-health architecture should accommodate diverse cultural understandings of well-being while remaining grounded in scientific evidence, clinical responsibility, and human rights. Integrating Traditional Chinese mind–body perspectives, family and community participation, and responsibly governed AI offers a potential model for more culturally responsive and participatory mental-health promotion. By connecting healthcare, families, communities, public authorities, and technology developers, the framework seeks to strengthen psychological resilience, preserve social participation across the life course, and contribute to more equitable and humane health systems.

items.title: Colonial mediations and sovereign possibilities: a synthesis-derived decolonial heuristic layered equity framework for equitable generative AI integration in K-12 and higher education
items.abstract: Purpose This critical integrative synthesis examines generative AI integration in K-12 and higher education through an explicit decolonial lens. It focuses on how colonial mediations shape opportunities, challenges and strategies for equitable access and outcomes aligned with UN SDG 10. Design/methodology/approach Following a critical integrative review paradigm that fuses the integrative logic of Whittemore and Knafl (2005) with reflexive thematic analysis (Braun and Clarke, 2006) and decolonial theory, 58 sources (2020–2026) were identified through systematic search and purposive theoretical sampling. Sources prioritizing structural critique, Global South perspectives, K-12 evidence gaps, output-level neocolonial patterns and contextual agency were retained. Sources were appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool and analyzed through a seven-phase relational mapping protocol that translated thematic codes into the layered architecture of the Decolonial Heuristic Layered Equity Framework (DHLEF). Robustness of core pathways was confirmed through sensitivity analyses. Findings Three interdependent themes – transformative opportunities, interlinked challenges and enabling strategies – emerge when read through decolonial theory. Opportunities appear as outer potential outcomes mediated by challenges whose effects are conditioned by data colonialism, epistemic colonialism, infrastructure dependence, governance colonialism and output-level neocolonial patterns. Strategies achieve moderating effects most effectively when reframed as sovereignty practices, including contextual hacking and language sovereignty. The DHLEF renders these colonial mediations visible in hypothesized relational pathways and supplies a context-differentiated implementation roadmap grounded in empirical evidence from low- and middle-income countries (LMIC) and K-12 contexts. Research limitations/implications Reliance on secondary and grey literature limits depth and generalizability. The DHLEF remains a synthesis-derived heuristic whose pathways constitute propositions requiring empirical validation through longitudinal and intersectional designs. The synthesis provides a transparent foundation for structural analysis rather than prescriptive protocols. Practical implications The DHLEF supplies institutions and policymakers with a context-sensitive, non-prescriptive heuristic for navigating generative AI integration. It enables differentiated decision-making by educational level and geopolitical resource setting, positioning sovereignty-oriented practices – offline-first tools, community governance and Indigenous data protocols – as conditional moderators rather than sequential prerequisites. Educators and technology providers can apply the framework to diagnose infrastructure dependence, epistemic bias and accessibility barriers prior to deployment, while prioritizing institutional support structures empirically shown to strengthen equitable outcomes in low-resource and K-12 environments. Implementation remains iterative and locally calibrated rather than universally prescribed. Social implications By rendering colonial mediations analytically central, the DHLEF advances structural justice rather than distributional inclusion alone, interrupting asymmetries in knowledge validation and educational opportunity. It positions sovereignty practices – contextual hacking, language sovereignty, community data governance and offline-first infrastructures – as necessary interruptions of data, epistemic and infrastructural extraction, with particular urgency for marginalized learners in Global South and low-resource contexts. The framework reframes equitable GenAI integration as an ongoing political and ethical project of refusal and resurgence, rather than a technical optimization problem, thereby aligning educational practice with the structural demands of UN SDG 10. Originality/value The DHLEF advances understanding by converting thematic synthesis into a relational structure that makes colonial mediations analytically central. It extends prior static ethics and education frameworks through decolonial integration and synthesis-derived pathways. It incorporates contextual differentiation by educational level and geopolitical setting, positions 2025–2026 trends as amplifiers of colonial dynamics and offers a tool for equitable GenAI integration that centers sovereignty rather than diffusion. The framework resolves three persistent tensions in existing scholarship: the absence of dynamic relational modelling, the dominance of distributional over structural equity framings and Northern-centric biases that have limited applicability to Global South and K-12 contexts.

items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Three Large Language Models in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Using a Clinical Vignette-Based Rubric
items.abstract: Background: Large language models (LLMs) can generate clinically relevant information, but safety-related performance in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) remains insufficiently characterised. We compared GPT-5.5 Instant (ChatGPT), Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3.5 Flash through their free-tier web interfaces across diagnostic acuity, guideline adherence, patient safety/red-flag recognition and hallucination-related reliability. Methods: Twelve SLE clinical vignettes were submitted to all three interfaces in May 2026 (36 single-pass responses). Two blinded specialists independently assessed the outputs using a study-developed four-domain rubric (composite range, 4–20). Inter-rater reliability was evaluated using quadratic-weighted Cohen’s κ. Paired comparisons across the shared vignettes used Friedman tests with Kendall’s W and post hoc Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm adjustment. Results: Inter-rater κ ranged from 0.754 to 0.893. Friedman tests showed between-interface differences for patient safety/red-flag recognition (χ2(2) = 9.571, p = 0.008, W = 0.399), hallucination-related reliability (χ2(2) = 6.500, p = 0.039, W = 0.271) and composite score (χ2(2) = 8.140, p = 0.017, W = 0.339), but not diagnostic acuity (p = 0.926) or guideline adherence (p = 0.175). Claude scored higher than ChatGPT and Gemini for patient safety (Holm-adjusted p = 0.0176 for both) and composite score (Holm-adjusted p = 0.0469 for both). No hallucination-related pairwise comparison remained significant after Holm adjustment. Conclusions: Within this exploratory, 12-vignette paired evaluation, the Claude interface received higher safety and composite ratings, but these observations do not establish generalisable model superiority or real-world clinical safety. The findings are specific to the tested May 2026 model versions and require independent replication.

items.title: Comparing ChatGPT Assessments Based on Transcripts and Screenshots with Anesthesiologists’ Evaluations of Ultrasound-Guided Abdominal Wall Block Videos: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Digital video-sharing platforms are widely used in anesthesia education, but the educational quality of ultrasound-guided abdominal wall block (UAWB) videos is heterogeneous. This cross-sectional study assessed agreement between a large language model (LLM) and experienced anesthesiologists in evaluating UAWB videos on YouTube. Seventy-five videos covering five UAWB techniques were independently evaluated by two anesthesiologists and ChatGPT version 5.2 using a researcher-developed 10-item Educational Content Checklist (ECC), DISCERN, the Global Quality Scale (GQS), and JAMA benchmark criteria. The LLM received each video’s full transcript, metadata screenshot, and 5–9 procedural screenshots rather than the full video. Human–LLM scores were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and agreement was quantified using intraclass correlation coefficients. Total scores did not differ significantly for the ECC (median 34 vs. 32; p = 0.168), DISCERN (54 vs. 54; p = 0.347), GQS (4 vs. 4; p = 0.469), or JAMA criteria (2 vs. 2; p = 0.865). However, agreement was limited: moderate for ECC (ICC = 0.576, 95% CI 0.404–0.709) and JAMA (ICC = 0.529, 95% CI 0.343–0.674), and poor for GQS (ICC = 0.495, 95% CI 0.303–0.648) and DISCERN (ICC = 0.357, 95% CI 0.146–0.538). In exploratory item-level analyses, differences emerged in vascular safety, needle technique, and indications. The absence of significant differences in total scores should not be interpreted as equivalence. LLM-assisted pre-screening is a potential application that requires prospective evaluation, and the present findings do not support replacing expert assessment with LLM evaluation, particularly for dynamic, safety-critical technical content.

items.title: Complementing Text Based Moderation with Multimodal Grounding: Detecting Fraudulent Inducement Behaviors on Short Video Platforms
items.abstract: Short video platforms have become a primary channel for black and gray industry operations in internet finance, where inducements such as prompts to like, follow, join private chat groups, or click external links frequently steer users toward fraud. Because such videos are short, dynamic, and often convey intent through fleeting visual cues rather than stable text, a moderation system must guarantee detection recall and localize the offending segment so reviewers inspect only the relevant clip. Existing OCR+LLM pipelines transcribe on-screen text frame by frame and classify the transcript, but exploit only textual information. Many inducements are conveyed through visual cues OCR cannot observe, and keyframe-based localization cannot recover precise temporal boundaries. We explore OCR+MLLM, which augments the text pipeline with a Multimodal Large Language Model, and compare three routes: OCR+LLM, OCR+MLLM, and a large zero-shot MLLM, along detection, latency, token consumption, and deployment complexity. OCR preserves the text signal that guarantees recall, while the MLLM jointly performs OCR-grounded discrimination and temporal grounding, localizing both textual and non-textual inducements. We construct a dataset of 2,419 internet finance short videos (66.49 hours) with 3,194 annotated events across four categories, and study reward design for RL-based grounding under class imbalance. We report two findings: auxiliary reward terms are exploited through reward hacking, and stronger localization rewards degrade class-balanced detection. We therefore design a recall-weighted F2 localization reward with class-balanced resampling. Experiments show OCR+MLLM localizes better than the keyframe OCR+LLM baseline (mIoU 26.52 vs. 14.49) and detects non-textual inducements that text-only pipelines miss, while maintaining 67.0 percent macro recall.

items.title: Conformal Gating of Extracted Factor Vectors in LLM Signal Pipelines under Delayed Labels and Regime Shift: A Simulation Study
items.abstract: Language model pipelines extract multi-dimensional factor vectors from financial text, but a trading desk needs to know when an extracted vector can be trusted. Audit labels arrive late, errors cluster in stress regimes, and error scale shifts after model or prompt updates. We evaluate a conformal gate on the extraction layer in a seeded simulation (300 firms, 60 quarters, 200 replications) with heavy-tailed errors, regime stress, a structural break and a two-quarter audit lag. Per-dimension 90% intervals cover the full eight-dimension vector only 43 to 48% of the time, while a max-score construction reaches 89.8% before the break with intervals 20 to 26% narrower than Bonferroni. Calibration frozen at go-live falls to 79.9% joint coverage after the break. Rolling, weighted and delayed-feedback adaptive calibration recover 88.2 to 89.8% on average, but no label-driven method protects the quarters just after a shift. As a risk control, the gate holds the error rate among accepted signals near 10% after the break, the adaptive protocols accept only 25 to 35% of signals, and the gate lowers risk-adjusted return in this design. As a risk control, the adaptive gates reject most signals after the break, accepting only 25 to 35% in the main study, and gating lowers risk-adjusted return in this design. A label-free drift monitor flags 83.5% of abrupt breaks in the quarter they occur, against 2.5% for label-based monitoring, but under gradual drift it flags only 3.5%, so its advantage but in the supplementary simulation code, where it flags 78.5% of abrupt breaks, it flags only 3.5% under gradual drift, so its advantage is specific to abrupt breaks. To test whether these mechanisms appear with a real extractor, we run a pilot that extracts seven financial fields from the earnings press releases of 492 S&P 500 companies the earnings press releases of 492 large US companies from an S&P 500 earnings-call dataset with an open-weight model and scores each figure against the SEC XBRL-reported value. Extraction is accurate for most figures, 94.9% within 1% once reference-label errors in the XBRL tags are corrected, and most of the figures first scored as errors turned out to be label errors rather than misreading. items.abstract: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) and cyber-physical control systems deployed in mission-critical environments present severe operational risks due to stochastic hallucinations, non-deterministic drift, and a lack of hard formal safety guarantees. Concurrently, theoretical breakthroughs in harmonic analysis -specifically OpenAI’s 2026 proof of Sogge’s local smoothing conjecture for the Euclidean wave equation (n ≥ 2) - have established continuous analytical bounds on wave focusing and energy concentration in Lp Sobolev spaces. In this monograph, we present a unified Data Physics framework bridging continuous Sobolev local smoothing with the discrete Layer 0 Invariant State Matrix (L0-ISM) architecture. We formalize the Helical Venturi Operator (Φv), which dynamically constricts logit sampling spaces based on Shannon entropy H(Pt), and map continuous boundary conditions onto a symmetric 19-state bounded lattice S ∈ {-9, ..., 0, ..., +9}. Using an embedded Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT Z3 / CP-SAT) formal solver, we prove that quantized state trajectories can be formally verified in sub-millisecond latency (<0.35 ms). Any physical invariant violation or boundary saturation (|si| ≥ 9) triggers an immediate, deterministic hardware-level -999 HARD_STOP interdiction. We demonstrate that L0-ISM provides an unbreachable safety envelope for real-time AI and critical infrastructure (e.g., mCDU cooling loops), eliminating matrix-lag and replacing soft prompt heuristics with mathematical certainty.

items.title: CoSTA: Co-Evolving Self-Play Timeline Agents for Complex Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering
items.abstract: Complex Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering (TKGQA) involves more than retrieving facts: the timestamp or validity interval of one fact can constrain the search for another, while multiple intervals may jointly determine the answer. Existing single-agent TKGQA methods typically investigate these facts within a single reasoning context, where evidence from different event histories can become interleaved and distractors can misdirect subsequent retrieval. Distributing investigations across agents can separate event-specific evidence into distinct contexts, but effective collaboration must still be learned because question decomposition, subtask investigation, and evidence synthesis are interdependent. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{Co}-Evolving \textbf{S}elf-Play \textbf{T}imeline \textbf{A}gents (CoSTA), which organizes facts into navigable timelines, delegates investigations to workers, and uses a coordinator to synthesize their original timestamped observations. CoSTA initializes a shared policy through role-conditioned distillation and jointly optimizes both roles through co-evolving self-play with final-answer rewards. Across three benchmarks, CoSTA achieves state-of-the-art overall performance, with particularly strong gains on complex multi-fact questions, while its compact variants outperform the evaluated closed-source LLM agents.

items.title: Creative Assignments and Who Gets Left Behind: A Systematic Review of Inclusion Readiness in Generative AI Teaching Practices in Business and Technology Higher Education
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) assignments are spreading rapidly in business and technology higher education, yet published accounts rarely report whether every student can take part on fair terms. This systematic review audited published GenAI assignments against the social, economic, institutional and environmental dimensions of pedagogical sustainability. Following PRISMA 2020, OpenAlex (2023–2026) was searched, 1092 peer-reviewed records were screened and 191 studies were included. Each assignment was coded for its creative family, access and fairness provisions, ethics content and assessment, and scored on a 0–5 inclusion-readiness index. An AI system served as primary coder; a human coder double-coded 30 studies and the author adjudicated all disagreements. Most assignments used GenAI as a tutor or thinking partner (52%). Provisions were scarce: 27% ensured free access, 2% offered a non-AI alternative task and 2% addressed disability. Privacy (53%) and opt-out (35%) appeared mainly as research-ethics safeguards rather than design features. Mean inclusion readiness was 1.30 of 5 (0.75 on design-only coding). Only one study in seven taught GenAI ethics, and environmental cost was taught once. Business courses favored choice and language support; technology courses favored central access. The index offers a measurable design and reporting checklist for sustainable GenAI pedagogy.

items.title: Crisis Leadership and Collaborative Governance in Forest and Land Fire Management: A Systematic Literature Review Using the TCCM–ADO Framework
items.abstract: Forest and land fires require leadership, interorganizational coordination, information management, resource mobilization, and community participation. Yet research on wildfire leadership, cross-jurisdictional collaboration, firefighter safety, and forest-and-land-fire governance differs in context, unit of analysis, and outcome measures, which limits comparability. This article presents a systematic literature review of 51 studies published in 2015–2026 (43 core and 8 comparator articles), selected from 447 Scopus records (440 after deduplication) records and reported following PRISMA 2020. The literature is mapped with the Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methods (TCCM) framework and synthesized with the Antecedents–Decisions/Practices–Outcomes (ADO) framework. In the response phase, the most widely coded themes are strategic communication and shared situational awareness (22 articles) and cross-actor coordination and resource negotiation (20 articles). The most widely coded constraint is resource scarcity, time pressure, workload, and fatigue (23 articles), while open information flow and negotiated interdependence each appear as supporting factors in 19 articles. These counts indicate thematic coverage, not effect sizes or causal evidence. The review identifies nine gaps, chiefly the need to link leader competencies and governance conditions to collaborative mechanisms and to operational, safety, and socio-ecological outcomes; to understand power asymmetries; and to test the transferability of wildfire models to Indonesia. The article proposes an integrative ADO model and nine propositions for comparative, longitudinal, and mixed-methods research.

items.title: Critical thinking dispositions and perceived support-dependence discrepancy in GenAI-assisted learning: evidence from human–AI interaction pathways
items.abstract: Background Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can support academic performance while also creating a perceived gap between AI-supported task completion and independently available competence. This study examined how multidimensional critical thinking dispositions are associated with cognitive offloading, cognitive enhancement, and perceived support-dependence discrepancy (PSD) in GenAI-assisted learning. Methods A cross-sectional survey was administered through Wenjuanxing from March 15 to May 20, 2026, using stratified purposive sampling across six Chinese universities. Of 990 submitted questionnaires, 797 eligible and complete responses were retained. The hypothesized pathways were tested using structural equation modeling, with a separate observed-score moderation analysis for academic stress and additional robustness and measurement-model assessments. Results Inquisitiveness was positively associated with cognitive enhancement (β = 0.515, p < 0.001) and cognitive offloading (β = 0.270, p < 0.001). Open-mindedness (β = 0.091, p = 0.039) and systematicity (β = 0.096, p = 0.029) showed small positive associations with cognitive enhancement, whereas analyticity and truth-seeking were not significantly associated with either interaction pathway. Cognitive offloading (β = 0.448, p < 0.001) and cognitive enhancement (β = 0.207, p < 0.001) were positively associated with PSD. The Academic Stress × Cognitive Offloading interaction was not significant (β = 0.048, p = 0.123; delta R-squared = 0.002). Alternative CFA specifications, a common-method-factor analysis, and reliability sensitivity analyses yielded broadly consistent focal conclusions, while the HTMT assessment provided qualified evidence of discriminant validity. Conclusion Critical thinking dispositions showed heterogeneous associations with GenAI interaction pathways, and both offloading and enhancement were associated with perceived support-dependent competence gaps. Because the outcome was measured with a single self-report item and the design was cross-sectional, the findings indicate statistical associations rather than objectively verified overconfidence, calibration bias, or causal effects.

items.title: Cross-linguistic differences in responses to patient queries on osteonecrosis of the femoral head between English and Chinese-oriented large language models: a semantically matched bilingual cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs) are capable of providing health information and consultation to patients with osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH). However, owing to imbalances in the linguistic distribution of their training corpora, the quality, readability, and safety profiles of outputs generated by the same model may vary across language settings. Objective This study aimed to compare bilingual responses to ONFH patient queries generated by six state-of-the-art flagship LLMs, comprising three English-oriented models (ChatGPT-5.6-Sol, Gemini-3.1-Pro, and Claude-Fable-5) and three Chinese-oriented models (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Qwen3.7-Max, and Doubao-Seed-2.1-Pro), and to multidimensionally evaluate their cross-linguistic capabilities for generating medical information in terms of information quality, actionability, clinical accuracy, safety risk, hallucination, and readability. Methods A question set comprising 36 semantically distinct patient queries regarding ONFH was developed, yielding 72 semantically matched English–Chinese paired prompts. Six state-of-the-art flagship LLMs were evaluated. Information quality was assessed using the Global Quality Score (GQS), DISCERN, the Quality Assessment of Medical Artificial Intelligence (QAMAI), and the 20-item Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP-20). Actionability was assessed using the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials (PEMAT-P), while clinical accuracy was evaluated using a 5-point Likert scale. Safety risk was assessed using a graded classification framework, and prespecified criteria were established for identifying hallucinations. Readability was evaluated using language-specific readability metrics for English and Chinese responses. Statistical analyses included the Friedman test, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and Spearman correlation analysis. Results A total of 432 responses generated by LLMs were included in this study, and good-to-excellent inter-rater reliability was observed for all evaluation indicators. Significant between-model differences in actionability and clinical accuracy were identified among the six models under both English and Chinese response conditions (all p < 0.05). Furthermore, clinical accuracy exhibited high cross-linguistic stability. ChatGPT-5.6-Sol showed high actionability and a relatively low frequency of Level 1 minor safety-related omissions under the English-language condition, whereas switching to Chinese was accompanied by reduced actionability and an increased frequency of Level 1 omissions. All observed nonzero safety events were Level 1 minor omissions; no Level 2 or Level 3 unsafe responses were identified in either language condition. Responses generated by all six models in both languages failed to reach the prespecified readability threshold for patient education. Conclusion The six LLMs showed significant inter-model differences in the actionability and clinical accuracy of responses to ONFH-related patient health queries in both English and Chinese settings, while clinical accuracy demonstrated favorable cross-linguistic stability. Notably, none of the six-model outputs met the applicable readability threshold for patient-targeted health education under either language condition. In clinical practice, model selection, prompting-language effects and hallucination-related risks should be comprehensively considered when deploying LLMs to deliver health information for patients with ONFH. At the present stage, LLM-generated content intended for direct patient-facing education requires cautious evaluation and human oversight.

This method realizes the quantitative management of semantic drift of accounting terms, enhances the international comparability of accounting information, and promotes the transformation of accounting linguistics to computational social science paradigm. Through real-time terminology governance, the framework reduces the burden of manual audit of accounting supervision institutions and reduces compliance risks.

items.title: Crystoria: A Large-Scale Crystal Dataset Linking Thermodynamic and Dynamical Stability for Materials AI
items.abstract: Large-scale crystal databases have transformed materials discovery by making millions of structures and thermodynamic properties accessible to materials informatics. Yet dynamical stability remains sparsely characterized at a comparable scale because its evaluation is substantially more computationally demanding than conventional structure and energy calculations. This mismatch creates a critical gap between the rapidly expanding crystal-structure space and the physical information available for materials research and machine learning. Here we introduce Crystoria, a large-scale crystal dataset designed to bring dynamical stability to the scale of modern materials data. We construct Crystoria by systematically curating low-energy and metastable inorganic crystals, standardizing their structural identities, and combining machine-learning-accelerated structural relaxation with phonon-based dynamical screening. The resulting dataset contains 2,649,640 crystal structures, spanning 89 elements, 219 of the 230 space groups, and primitive cells containing 1-48 atoms. Among them, 1,793,353 structures (67.68%) are classified as dynamically stable, revealing substantial variation in dynamical stability across chemical and crystallographic space. By bringing dynamical stability to the scale of millions of crystal structures, Crystoria provides a physically grounded foundation for materials artificial intelligence (AI) and enables systematic exploration of the dynamical crystal landscape.

items.title: Current practices, challenges, and future directions in subcutaneous oncology monoclonal antibody delivery: a qualitative study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Subcutaneous oncology monoclonal antibodies (SCOmAbs) offer significant benefits compared to intravenous formulations, including reduced administration time and potential for self-administration. However, little has been published on real-world preparation and administration practices with these novel formulations. Methods This was a qualitative, exploratory study of 30 participants (10 patients receiving SCOmAbs, 10 nurses, and 10 pharmacists/pharmacy technicians) across various U.S. healthcare facilities. One-on-one, in-depth interviews examined current practices, pain points, device integration potential, projected impact of increased SCOmAb adoption, and perspectives on home administration. Results Findings revealed considerable variability in SCOmAb preparation and administration practices. While preparation methods generally aligned with typical parenteral workflows, notable deviations included bedside preparation by nurses (7/30), use of syringe pump modules (3/19), and one case of patient self-administration at home. Most participants utilized closed-system transfer devices (12/22) despite inconsistent hazardous drug treatment between facilities. Administration challenges included ergonomic difficulties for nurses during manual push (5/9 reporting physical discomfort) and variable injection techniques to accommodate patient comfort. Nurses reported significant workflow impact from being “tethered” to patients during administration, which could require staffing adjustments as SCOmAb frequency increases. Most patients (6/9) expressed interest in home administration for potential time savings and flexibility, though concerns about training, support, and safety were common. Conclusions As SCOmAb utilization expands, facilities may face barriers associated with increased demand that could necessitate innovative solutions. To leverage the full potential of SCOmAb products, developers should consider how next generation product presentations might minimize identified pain points, streamline administration, and facilitate safe transition to home self-administration. Delivery device integration, whether through prefilled syringes, portable infusion pumps, or other delivery systems, may address current challenges but requires careful consideration of facility infrastructure, product complexity and usability, workflow impact, and patient training requirements.

items.title: Cyberlogic-enabled Thinking Space: a closed-loop human-cyber cognitive architecture in CPST
items.abstract: Human–AI collaboration in Cyber–Physical–Social–Thinking (CPST) environments requires coordination among perception, reasoning, human judgment, and governance. This paper proposes Cyberlogic-enabled Thinking Space (CyTS), a conceptual governance-centric architecture organized through Entity, Mapping, Reasoning, and Governance layers. Its closed loop connects multimodal representation, heterogeneous reasoning, collaborative decisions, and controlled adaptation. The Entity layer provides operational descriptions rather than a sufficient ontology of cognition; logical consistency and predictive accuracy do not by themselves establish the causal validity of an action. CyTS therefore distinguishes associative, deductive, interventional, and exploratory claims and requires explicit assumptions, evidence provenance, uncertainty, and verification status at component interfaces. Structural causal models provide one implementable route, while equilibrium-based causal logic and proposals concerning brain–universe similarity and entangled machine thinking are examined as research perspectives with separate validation requirements. Governance mechanisms support privacy, accountability, human oversight, and runtime monitoring, including abstention when evidence or constraints are insufficient. Research hypotheses and evaluation protocols address causal transparency, decision quality, adaptation, cross-space coordination, and energy cost. Healthcare, education, and transportation scenarios illustrate the proposed workflow; they do not constitute empirical validation. CyTS contributes an auditable organizational framework and a testable implementation agenda, without claiming a completed theory of cognition or demonstrated performance gains.

items.title: DATA AS A FINANCIAL ASSET: HOW FINTECH COMPANIES USE CONSUMER BEHAVIOUR DATA FOR PERSONALISATION, RETENTION, AND REVENUE GROWTH
items.abstract: This study examines how FinTech companies transform consumer behaviour data into financial value through artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and hyper - personalisation. It explores how transactional, behavioural, and demographic data are collected, analysed,and converted into personalised financial products, recommendations, interfaces, and communication strategies. The study further evaluates how these practices influence customer retention, customer lifetime value, return on investment, average revenue per user, customer acquisition cost, and churn. Particular attention is given to machine learning, customer segmentation, recommendation systems, and predictive models used to anticipate consumer needs and improve engagement. The paper also considers the strategic role of data in product development, cross-selling, and marketing optimization. Alongside these benefits, it critically examines privacy, consent, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity, and regulatory compliance. The study concludes that AI-driven personalisation can create substantial commercial value in FinTech, but sustainable growth depends on transparent, secure, fair, and responsible use of consumer data over the long term.

items.title: Data Breaches in Government Digital Public Services: A Systematic Mapping of Research and Governance Challenges (2015–2025)
items.abstract: Background: The rapid digital transformation of public services has increased the collection and use of citizens’ personal data, intensifying concerns about data breaches in government-operated systems. However, existing research remains fragmented, with technical cybersecurity perspectives receiving greater attention than governance and public administration perspectives. Objective: This study aims to systematically map global research on data breaches in digital public services from 2015 to 2025 and identify theoretical and governance gaps relevant to the Indonesian context. Methods: A systematic literature review guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines was combined with bibliometric and scientometric analyses of publications indexed in Scopus. Descriptive bibliometric analysis and author keyword co-occurrence mapping using VOSviewer were conducted on 1,169 open-access documents, while 62 articles meeting the final eligibility criteria were examined through qualitative synthesis. Results: The findings reveal an increase in research output and six thematic clusters. Cybersecurity and data security had the highest keyword occurrence (235), whereas privacy, ethics, and data protection exhibited the greatest total link strength (457). Governance, institutional accountability, organizational capacity, and public trust remain comparatively less integrated into technical cybersecurity research. Conclusion: This study reconceptualizes data breaches in digital public services as sociotechnical governance challenges involving technological vulnerabilities, institutional capacity, regulatory arrangements, and public trust. The findings provide a conceptual foundation for strengthening public-sector data governance in Indonesia while highlighting the need for empirical validation and further comparative research.

items.title: Deep learning-based self-supervised detection and localization of magnetic resonance imaging anomalies in artificial intelligence-supported radiotherapy workflows
items.abstract: Background and purpose: Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into radiotherapy workflows, yet it remains vulnerable to out-of-distribution image data that can introduce unexpected behavior in clinical tasks. Deep learning (DL)-based anomaly detection for pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains limited and transparent evaluation for full automation is lacking. This study aimed to develop two self-supervised anomaly-detection framework variations in radiotherapy for pelvic and brain MRI. Materials and methods : A two-stage self-supervised DL-framework was trained separately for pelvic and brain MRI utilizing three public datasets. The first stage compressed normal image data into discrete representations, and a second stage modeled the representation distribution. Anomaly-evidence was obtained by combining perceptual image differences with token-surprisal scores via negative log-likelihood estimation. Automated detection was evaluated for two anatomical cohorts: pelvis, encompassing both synthetic global anomalies and real clinical anomalies, and brain, comprising clinically annotated anomalies. Performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). For each cohort, a subset of normal images was reserved for analysis. Results: Promising exploratory performance across evaluation cohorts was obtained. AUCs were 0.97 (95% CI 0.96–0.99) for synthetic pelvic anomalies, 0.95 (95% CI 0.90–1.00) for clinical pelvic anomalies, and 0.81 (95% CI 0.74–0.87) for brain anomalies. Qualitative heatmap analysis showed spatial agreement between detected anomalies and reference annotations. Conclusions: The framework variations showed promising anomaly detection performance across pelvic and brain MRI, supporting its potential for automated MRI quality control in radiotherapy. Heatmap-based visualization further improved interpretability by spatially localizing detected anomalies.

items.title: Deferral to AI in an Observational Causal Inference Task
items.abstract: Experts increasingly use AI agents for open-ended work that requires judgment and has no ground-truth answers. Studies of AI-assisted decision-making usually define over-reliance as accepting a recommendation that is plainly wrong. In open-ended work, over-reliance can also mean handing judgment to the agent, knowingly or not [1]. These judgment calls will likely remain important as AI capabilities improve. Because they lack ground truth, they are hard to benchmark or train on. Experts may therefore keep using agents for the decisions where the agents' reliability and the right level of reliance are hardest to assess. Observational causal inference is one such setting where key identifying assumptions often cannot be tested from the available data. Independent expert teams given the same dataset and hypothesis have regularly reached different conclusions [2, 3, 4]. To test whether an assistant's hidden preference shifts expert decisions, we run a randomized controlled trial in which causal-inference practitioners (N ≈ 50) complete a 45-60 minute program-evaluation task in a monitored workspace, each working with an AI assistant randomly assigned to favor one side of five analytical decisions required to complete the task. Participants do not know that these decisions are the focus of the study. The primary outcome compares participants' choices across the assistant's assigned sides: how often the final choice aligns with the side the assistant favors. Secondary outcomes test whether the assigned side shifts the participant's final recommendation and whether participants switch sides after the assistant voices an opposed lean. We specify the estimators, exclusions, masked outcome coding, and deviations log in advance.

items.title: DES-JEPA: Learning a Shared Vocabulary for High-Dimensional Discrete Event Sequences
items.abstract: Temporal foundation models such as Chronos and TimesFM generalize across domains through a shared numerical observation space. In contrast, discrete event sequences (DESs), including operational event logs or patient clinical-event trajectories, have domain-specific event vocabularies whose labels lack a consistent correspondence across domains. Beyond this lack of consistency, the number of distinct events in real-world settings is high enough to challenge both classical temporal point process modeling and current in-context foundation inference models such as FIM-PP. Critically, current foundation models for DESs are limited to a small, fixed number of event types, restricting their applicability to realistic, high-dimensional event streams. To address this, we propose two complementary modules: (i) DES-JEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture that learns a shared discrete vocabulary from synthetic stochastic processes with unaligned event vocabularies; and (ii) DES-PFN, a discrete event sequence prior-fitted network that reuses the learned vocabulary for in-context next-event prediction. Without task-specific fine-tuning, this framework achieves competitive zero-shot performance on eight unseen real-world datasets and scales up to 700 distinct event types.

items.title: DESAFIOS NA PROTEÇÃO DOS DIREITOS AUTORAIS NO CONTEXTO DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NO BRASIL: ENTRE A INOVAÇÃO E A INSEGURANÇA JURÍDICA
items.abstract: Este artigo analisa a relação entre os direitos autorais e a inteligência artificial no ordenamento jurídico brasileiro, com foco no uso de obras protegidas no treinamento de sistemas e na autoria, proteção e responsabilização relativas aos conteúdos gerados. A pesquisa é qualitativa, bibliográfica e documental, de abordagem jurídico-dogmática e comparativa, com análise de legislação, doutrina, jurisprudência e experiências regulatórias nacionais e estrangeiras. Os resultados demonstram que não há vazio normativo geral: a autoria é atribuída à pessoa física pelo art. 11 da Lei nº 9.610/1998, enquanto a proteção de resultados produzidos com auxílio de IA depende de contribuição humana criativa demonstrável. As principais lacunas concentram-se na disciplina da mineração de textos e dados, na documentação dos conteúdos utilizados no treinamento e na definição de critérios para aferição da contribuição humana. Conclui-se que a dificuldade probatória constitui obstáculo central à tutela autoral, tornando relevantes mecanismos de transparência e proveniência, além do aperfeiçoamento legislativo em discussão no Projeto de Lei nº 2.338/2023. CHALLENGES IN PROTECTING COPYRIGHT IN THE CONTEXT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BRAZIL: BETWEEN INNOVATION AND LEGAL UNCERTAINTY ABSTRACT This article analyzes the relationship between copyright and artificial intelligence (AI) within the Brazilian legal system, focusing on the use of copyrighted works in the training of AI systems and on issues of authorship, protection, and liability concerning generated content. The study adopts a qualitative, bibliographic, and documentary approach, employing a doctrinal legal approach and comparative methodology to examine legislation, legal scholarship, case law, and domestic and foreign regulatory approaches. The results demonstrate that there is no general regulatory vacuum: under Article 11 of Law No. 9,610/1998, authorship is attributed to natural persons, while copyright protection for AI-assisted outputs depends on a demonstrable creative human contribution. The main legal gaps concern the regulation of text and data mining, the documentation of content used in training, and the establishment of criteria for assessing human contribution. It is concluded that evidentiary difficulties constitute a central obstacle to copyright protection, highlighting the relevance of transparency and content provenance mechanisms, as well as legislative improvements under discussion in Bill No. 2,338/2023.

items.title: Design and Development of Battery Operated Weeder for Wetland Rice
items.abstract: Background: Wetland rice cultivation requires effective inter-row weed management, but manual weeding is labour-intensive and conventional powered machines can be difficult to operate in puddled soil. Aim: To design and develop a battery-powered weeder that provides a lightweight, economical, ergonomic and eco-friendly machinery solution to reduce dependence on manual labour in wetland rice fields. Place and Duration of Study: Department of Farm Machinery and Power Engineering, SVCAET & RS, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur, Chhattisgarh, India, during 2025–2026. Methodology: The machine was powered by a 650 W DC motor paired with a 27 V, 30 Ah lithium iron phosphate battery system. Key structural components incorporated into the design included a mild steel chassis, rotating stainless-steel blades, a worm gear transmission system, a control unit and a dedicated floating mechanism. Results: The dimensions of the developed weeder were 780 × 560 × 1400 mm, with a total weight of 17.10 kg. Theoretical battery-runtime estimation indicated approximately 1.24 hours, while the ideal full-recharge time was estimated at approximately 2.4 hours for a 12.5 A charging current. The fabrication cost of the developed unit was estimated at ₹29,840. Conclusion: A lightweight ( ) battery-operated wetland weeder powered by a DC motor and a lithium iron phosphate battery pack was successfully designed, fabricated, and put into operation for inter-row weed management in puddled rice fields.

items.abstract: This study aimed to design a KLPCM application for reviewing the completeness of inpatient medical-record documentation at the West Java Provincial Occupational Health Hospital using Microsoft Visual Studio 2010. The system was developed using the prototyping method. The study produced a flowmap, context diagram, level-0 Data Flow Diagram (DFD), and Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD), which were implemented as a Visual Basic .NET-based prototype comprising a login form, main menu, two medical-record completeness input forms, and an automatically calculated eight-item monthly report form. Master data were stored in Microsoft Access, while review data and reports were stored in Excel. The application was designed because KLPCM results at the hospital were still recorded directly in Excel, resulting in repetitive data entry, susceptibility to errors, and time-consuming monthly recapitulation, which may affect staff performance, operational efficiency, and service quality. The prototype should be tested with a larger number of staff, user feedback should be collected for subsequent development, and the data should be migrated to a database before official implementation.

items.title: Designing Embedded Intelligence through Co-Design Substrates Optimization and System Assurance
items.abstract: Embedded intelligence places sensing, inference, adaptation, and decision making inside physical systems limited by energy, memory, latency, cost, and reliability. This narrative review examines the field along four connected axes: hardware and software co-design, computational substrates, optimization at the model, mapping, and system levels, and applications in industrial automation, automotive electronics, healthcare monitoring, and the Internet of Things. Timing, safety, and security are treated as requirements that cut across all four axes. The review separates embedded intelligence from constrained on-device machine learning and from edge artificial intelligence, and it frames deployment as a cross-layer problem in which model quality, hardware mapping, timing, energy, security, and adaptation constrain one another. Two literature-based case studies, one on a field-programmable gate arrayand one on distributed microcontrollers, show how a gain at one layer produces a cost at another. A recomputation of the efficiency ratios reported in one of the studies shows why measurement boundaries and metric definitions must be declared. Six research priorities are derived from limitations that recur in the reviewed sources: lifecycle energy accounting, assurance of learned components, security of distributed deployments, reproducible benchmarking, portable deployment toolchains, and concept drift after deployment. Each priority is paired with a research direction and evaluation criteria for later studies. The evidence consists mainly of surveys, analytical studies, and laboratory implementations, so quantitative values are reported as stated in the sources, recomputed values are labeled as such, and approaches are not ranked. The proposed formulations and criteria are conceptual.

items.title: Developing a multi-level human-centered design framework for digital health implementation: a cross-project methodological synthesis
items.abstract: Background Digital health interventions have considerable potential to improve healthcare access, quality, and efficiency. Despite increasing adoption, many interventions fail to achieve sustainable implementation or progress beyond pilot phases because they are insufficiently integrated with user needs, organizational workflows, and health system contexts. Although human-centered design (HCD) has improved the usability and acceptability of digital health technologies, its application frequently remains confined to early design activities and is rarely integrated with implementation science throughout the implementation lifecycle. Objective This study aimed to develop a multi-level, human-centered design framework informed by a cross-project methodological synthesis integrating participatory design and implementation science to support the design, implementation, evaluation, and scale-up of digital health interventions. Methods A cross-project methodological synthesis was conducted using complementary digital health implementation studies undertaken in Kenya. The empirical corpus included studies spanning adolescent mental health, neonatal clinical decision support, digital health infrastructure, generative artificial intelligence, and frugal digital health innovation. Framework development followed an iterative analytical process combining thematic synthesis, constant comparative analysis, and abductive reasoning. The synthesis organized recurring methodological themes into an integrated framework spanning user, workflow, and system perspectives across the digital health implementation lifecycle. Results The synthesis identified recurring methodological processes that consistently contributed to successful digital health implementation, including contextual understanding, participatory stakeholder engagement, iterative refinement, workflow integration, organizational readiness, governance, and sustainability. These findings informed the development of a multi-level framework structured around six iterative implementation phases: Understand, Co-design, Prototype, Evaluate, Implement, and Scale, and three interconnected analytical levels: user (micro), workflow (meso), and system (macro). The framework conceptualizes digital health implementation as a continuous sociotechnical process in which sustained adoption and scale-up depend upon coordinated alignment among these three levels throughout the implementation lifecycle. Conclusions This study advances human-centered design by integrating it with implementation science through an empirically derived, lifecycle-oriented methodological framework for digital health implementation. The proposed framework may provide researchers, developers, practitioners, and policymakers with a structured approach for designing, implementing, evaluating, and scaling digital health interventions while supporting sustainable, context-responsive, and equitable digital health transformation.

items.title: DEVELOPING CRITICAL THINKING SKILLS IN INTERMEDIATE EFL LEARNERS THROUGH TASK-BASED LANGUAGE TEACHING
items.abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of Task-Based Language Teaching (TBLT) in fostering critical thinking skills among intermediate-level English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners. A quasi-experimental design was employed with 64 intermediate EFL students randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 32) that received TBLT instruction and a control group (n = 32) that followed a conventional presentation-practice-production approach over a 12-week period. Critical thinking was measured using a modified California Critical Thinking Skills Test adapted for language learners and a task-based performance rubric assessing analysis, evaluation, inference, and argumentation. Results indicated statistically significant gains in the experimental group across all critical thinking dimensions (p < .01), with particularly strong improvements in analysis and evaluation. Qualitative data from learner reflective journals and classroom observations further revealed that authentic, meaning-focused tasks encouraged deeper cognitive engagement, perspective-taking, and reasoned decision-making. The findings suggest that carefully designed TBLT sequences can simultaneously advance linguistic competence and higher-order thinking skills. Implications for EFL curriculum design and teacher training are discussed.

items.title: Development and evaluation of X‐ray lithophanes as test objects for interventional procedure simulation
items.abstract: Abstract Background In the growing field of interventional radiology, emerging technologies implement the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to help tackle growing demands for treatment. Due to the anatomical differences in animals, volunteers offer the most realistic training and testing scenario, however safety considerations restrict rapid prototyping of these new technologies. Simulators have been a key facilitator in the testing of new technologies among numerous medical engineering studies, but often lack the realism to reliably test AI. Purpose This proof‐of‐concept study presents methods to create or enhance hyper‐realistic radiographic simulators that can effectively function with a medical‐grade AI software. Methods Iron‐filled plastic was used to three‐dimensionally (3D) print a series of blocks of heights up to 30 mm. By analyzing the intensities generated by different thicknesses of plastic, anonymous fluoroscopic images were turned into height maps (lithophanes) and 3D‐printed. A static scene from transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was then 3D‐printed and imaged with different presets using two different x‐ray systems for mathematical analysis. Lithophanes were then used as a radiographic background to experimental and commercial interventional simulators to test Caranx Medical's TAVIPILOT AI. Finally, fluoroscopies from 5 3D‐printed lithophanes were mixed with 5 real images and presented to 5 expert volunteers to establish their realism in a structured survey. Results The 3D‐printed x‐ray lithophanes test‐plates' radiographic appearance was rated as “Adequate” to “Good” across all fields of the survey, with participants praising their realism. The test‐plate was able to reliably recreate the TAVI scene in different x‐ray systems, with joint‐histogram correlation coefficients above 0.9, and global structural similarity above 0.8. The lithophanes were imaged as a standalone test plate and as a backing to dynamic TAVI interventional simulators; in both cases, TAVIPILOT AI responded to the simulator as if it was operating on a real anatomical image. Conclusions Lithophane plates present an easy‐to‐implement solution to recreate monoplane x‐ray scenes, which can be deployed to test software at the point of care with minimal logistical, ethical, or safety concerns. This study opens the door for a new range of interventional simulators able to recreate human‐like appearance to test AI, offering a non‐exclusive alternative to patient volunteers and anonymous data.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a routine metabolic screening model for current hyperuricemia among gas station workers in Guangxi, China: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Serum uric acid (SUA) measurement is the direct basis for identifying current hyperuricemia (HUA). We developed a non-SUA screening model for situations in which routine occupational health information is already available but a contemporaneous SUA result is temporarily unavailable, delayed, or requires separate testing. Methods This cross-sectional study included 894 workers from 11 gas stations and related operational sites in Nanning, Guangxi, China. Current HUA was defined as same-examination SUA > 420 µmol/L in both sexes. Twelve prespecified non-SUA candidate variables were considered; total cholesterol was excluded because of high redundancy and multicollinearity with LDL-C, leaving 11 candidates for least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) screening. Internal validation used 100 repetitions of site-grouped five-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using out-of-fold (OOF) predictions, discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, candidate screening thresholds, and bootstrap optimism correction. Results Among 894 participants, 169 (18.9%) had current HUA. Sex, waist circumference, triglycerides (TG), systolic blood pressure (SBP), and fasting blood glucose (FBG) met the prespecified selection-stability threshold and comprised the final model. The mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) across repeated site-grouped cross-validation was 0.858 (SD 0.004), and the pooled OOF AUC was 0.866 (95% CI, 0.838–0.893). The pooled OOF Brier score was 0.108, the calibration intercept was − 0.064 (95% CI, -0.322 to 0.192), and the calibration slope was 0.920 (95% CI, 0.791–1.077). At a 10% candidate probability threshold, sensitivity was 92.9%, specificity was 64.6%, and the negative predictive value was 97.5%. Conclusions The five-variable model estimates the probability of current HUA and may support prioritization of confirmatory SUA testing when a contemporaneous SUA result is unavailable. It does not replace direct SUA measurement or predict future incident HUA. Independent external validation is required before broader implementation.

items.title: Development and Preliminary Psychometric Evaluation of a Digital-Intelligence Literacy Self-Report Scale Among Students in Medical and Health-Related Programs
items.abstract: Medical students increasingly engage with interconnected digital systems, health data, and artificial intelligence (AI), but existing instruments vary in the aspects of digital, data, and AI literacy they assess in medical contexts. This study developed and initially evaluated the Chinese-language Digital-Intelligence Literacy Scale for Medical Students (DIL-MS). Following two rounds of consultation with 16 experts, a 34-item questionnaire was field-tested at one Chinese university. Of 1118 returned questionnaires, 710 were analyzed in non-overlapping exploratory (n = 344) and confirmatory (n = 366) subsamples. items.title: Development and preliminary validation of an AI acceptance scale for intercultural teaching and its cross-sectional associations with university teachers’ occupational wellbeing
items.abstract: Background University teachers’ occupational wellbeing and emotional exhaustion are relevant occupational-health concerns in higher education. As generative artificial intelligence becomes embedded in teaching work, AI acceptance may represent a perceived, context-specific appraisal of whether AI is usable for intercultural teaching tasks. This study developed a preliminary measure of AI acceptance for intercultural teaching and examined its cross-sectional associations with teacher resources and occupational-health indicators. Methods This two-sample cross-sectional study used Sample A to examine the empirical behavior of the AI Acceptance for Intercultural Teaching Scale and Sample B to test measurement validity and occupational health associations. IBM SPSS Statistics 27.0.1 was used for descriptive statistics, EFA, Cronbach’s alpha, correlations, and regression analyses. CFA and SEM were conducted in R 4.6.1 (lavaan 0.6.21, lavaan.mi 0.1.0, and mice 3.19.0) using robust maximum likelihood (MLR) estimation; CR and AVE were calculated from standardized CFA loadings, and HTMT from item correlations. Hypothesis tests used non-imputed scale-score regressions; multiple imputation (mice, m = 5) with D2-pooled CFA/SEM model tests served as sensitivity analysis, and indirect-association bootstrap intervals were sensitivity summaries rather than formal D2-pooled tests. Results The AITA items were suitable for factor analysis in Sample A (KMO = 0.940), but the exploratory loading pattern did not cleanly reproduce the theorized four TAM-based dimensions. In Sample B, the overall AITA score showed good internal consistency (alpha = 0.858), whereas the four subdimensions showed substantial overlap and weaker reliability and convergent-validity evidence. AI acceptance was positively associated with intercultural teaching self-efficacy and autonomous teaching motivation. Self-efficacy was associated with both occupational wellbeing and lower emotional exhaustion, whereas autonomous motivation was associated primarily with occupational wellbeing. Direct associations between AI acceptance and the occupational-health outcomes were not significant. Conclusion The present findings provide preliminary evidence for using the overall AITA score as a context-specific measure of AI acceptance in intercultural teaching. The results also show cross-sectional associations between AI acceptance and teacher-resource variables, but they do not establish causal effects, mediation, or intervention effectiveness. The four TAM-based dimensions should be treated as provisional content facets requiring further validation.
